subject: Clarify VPC seat vs host pricing, implementation cap, and staggered support credits
messages:
From: Greg Sullivan <greg@medbridge.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on VPC pricing model and support credits

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we're building the internal justification for a VPC/on-prem deployment, a few follow-ups from procurement on how you price the bundle:

1) Seat vs host: procurement wants to understand the delta if we license by end-user seats (agents) versus host nodes. Does Redwood have a recommended conversion metric (e.g., x seats per node) or a floating billing tolerance?

2) Implementation cap: they asked whether the one-time implementation charge can be capped at a fixed $ value if we push to a phased rollout across 3 hospitals.

3) Staggered support credits: we'd like to propose a schedule where support credits (for onboarding engineering time) are applied over the first 12 months rather than upfront. Is that something you can accept?

I've attached our procurement checklist and the rough timeline. Happy to schedule a call this week.

Best,
Greg Sullivan
VP of Product & Ops
MedBridge Health

Attachments: procurement-checklist.pdf (referenced), timeline.xlsx (referenced)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Can you:

- Vanessa: confirm whether we can structure the support credit schedule across months and any accounting constraints.
- Karthik: any technical caveats on phased rollout that would affect cost (e.g., extra staging nodes, parallel run costs).

Thanks — I'll loop back to Greg once we have proposed language.

— David
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-06T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on VPC pricing model and support credits

David — quick take from commercial:

Seat vs host pricing
- We generally offer both seat-based and host/node-based models. For MedBridge scale (~300 concurrent agents across 3 sites), our default conversion we use in quoting is: 1 host node per 50 concurrent agents for standard gen models; heavy LLM workloads (long context, high tokens) push that to 1:30.
- Proposed wording for SOW: "Pricing may be expressed in either Seats or Hosts. At signing, parties agree on the conversion factor (Seats-to-Hosts = X). During the term, usage that deviates by >20% from the baseline may trigger a commercial reconciliation at each 6-month milestone."

Implementation cap
- We can cap the implementation SOW at $150k for a phased rollout across the 3 hospitals, contingent on scope fidelity (no more than 3 on-site visits; remote work sampling allowed). If scope grows, overages billed at T&M with 30-day notice.

Staggered support credits
- We can amortize onboarding support credits over 12 months with these constraints: credits must be drawn monthly, unused credits expire after 12 months, and credits cannot be stacked against peak incident response SLAs. Accounting will need to treat the credits as a deferred revenue deduction.

I'll prepare a short appendix with the exact contract snippets and the conversion table.

— Marissa
Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-06T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on VPC pricing model and support credits

David/Marissa — operational note on support credits and implementation cap. From an Ops perspective, we can accept the $150k cap for implementation if the SOW includes:

- Phased rollout schedule with acceptance gates after each hospital onboard (Acceptance gates: smoke tests, traffic baseline, runbook sign-off).
- A minimum 30-day staging period on customer infra for us to validate KV cache and prefix caching behavior.
- A clause that additional parallel staging environments required by the customer will be charged separately.

On amortized support credits: absolutely doable. Suggestion for the contract language:
- "Support Credits: Customer will receive X hours of onboarding engineering support to be consumed over the first 12 months. Unused hours expire after month 12. Credits may be used for onboarding and knowledge transfer activities and shall not reduce required SLA incident response times."

Finally, Karthik — please confirm whether having staggered staging windows increases our engineering time materially (estimate in hours).

— Vanessa
Senior Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-06T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on VPC pricing model and support credits

Ops estimates — phased rollout across 3 hospitals with staggered windows:
- Baseline engineering for single-site rollout: 240 engineer-hours (setup, validation, runbooks).
- Additional sites (phased) add ~80 hours each if we can reuse configs and there are no custom integrations.
- If MedBridge requires parallel staging environments or extended on-site presence, add 120 hours per extra staging environment.

Net impact: under the proposed cap ($150k) we are tight but feasible if they accept the constraints Vanessa outlined. If they want parallel staging or heavy data migrations per site, ask for an overage bucket.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Greg Sullivan <greg@medbridge.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medbridge.com>
Date: 2026-04-08T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on VPC pricing model and support credits

David/Team — thanks for the clear answers and the proposed language. A few clarifications from procurement:

- The 1:50 conversion at baseline looks reasonable; procurement requests that we include a simple example table in the quote (seats -> hosts -> monthly unit cost) for the CFO.
- For the $150k implementation cap, procurement asks for a one-line clause that guarantees no surprise on-site fees beyond the three visits; they are ok with T&M overages if notified 30 days in advance.
- On staggered credits: we accept amortization over 12 months with monthly drawdown. We do want a short statement confirming credits won't be reallocated to cover operational incident responses in months 6–12.

If you can send a one-page pricing appendix and mark-up of the two SOW clauses by tomorrow, procurement will fast-track the PO.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Greg
VP Product & Ops
MedBridge Health
